featured.title: Nepal Flood Death Toll Surges Past 330 as Glacier Collapse Scale Becomes Clear
featured.excerpt: Scientists confirm an ice-rock avalanche, not an earthquake, triggered one of Nepal's worst natural disasters, with over 900 people still missing including dozens of Americans and 177 Indian pilgrims.
featured.image_caption: An aerial view shows houses buried under mud and debris following flash floods in Nepal on August 26, 2026. The floods killed over 330 people and left more than 900 missing across eight districts.
featured.nri_angle: 177 Indian pilgrims en route to Kailash Mansarovar are among the missing, 63 Americans unaccounted for, and downstream flooding prompted evacuations in Bihar — the disaster has direct implications for diaspora families across South Asia.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

editorial.title: Who Is Asha Sharma? The Wisconsin-Born Executive Who Never Made a Video Game — and Is Now Running Xbox
editorial.excerpt: Seven months after Microsoft handed her the Xbox controller, the former Instacart COO is cutting thousands of jobs, cutting Game Pass prices, and telling hard truths — guided by a mantra from her immigrant upbringing: clarity is kindness.
editorial.image_caption: Asha Sharma at the 2026 Xbox Showcase. She became CEO of Microsoft Gaming in February 2026, succeeding Phil Spencer.
editorial.nri_angle: Sharma's rise to the top of Xbox — and the racist backlash her appointment drew despite her Wisconsin birth — captures both the ascent and the friction of Indian-American leadership in 2026.
editorial.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: BofA Sees Chip Market Nearly Doubling to $3.2 Trillion by 2030, Names ETFs
just_in.excerpt: BofA’s Vivek Arya projects the semiconductor market nearly doubling by 2030, with memory leading and equipment spend more than doubling — naming Nvidia, AMD, Marvell and two chip-gear stocks plus five ETFs.
just_in.image_caption: A semiconductor wafer. Bank of America projects the global chip market could nearly double to $3.2 trillion by 2030.
just_in.nri_angle: For US-based Indian investors, BofA’s call frames the actionable AI-infrastructure trade: booked capacity through 2027, equipment spend doubling, and a named set of stocks and ETFs.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: JPMorgan Sticks With Chip-Equipment Leaders as AI Buildout Drives Tool Demand
just_in.excerpt: JPMorgan stays Overweight on Applied Materials, KLA and Lam Research — and Friday’s SOX action showed investors agree: chip-making tools are Wall Street’s preferred AI-buildout bet.
just_in.image_caption: Inside a semiconductor fabrication facility. JPMorgan is sticking with leading chip-equipment makers as the AI buildout drives tool demand.
just_in.nri_angle: For US-based Indian investors, Wall Street’s equipment-first AI thesis translates into a portfolio lens: the SOX’s equipment leaders are where JPMorgan and BofA see the most durable AI-buildout exposure.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: FSSAI Weighs National Ban on Analogue Paneer After State Consensus Push
just_in.excerpt: FSSAI chief Rajit Punhani will put a nationwide analogue paneer ban to state food safety commissioners on September 24 — eight states already prohibit it, and the regulator says paneer is nutritionally irreplaceable.
just_in.image_caption: Fresh paneer. India’s food safety regulator is weighing a national ban on analogue paneer after states reached consensus.
just_in.nri_angle: Diaspora families dining out in India — or buying paneer at home — get the clearest signal yet that the regulator wants fake paneer off plates nationwide, timed ahead of the Diwali festive rush.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Acharya Balkrishna Says Turmeric Milk Is Ayurveda’s Go-To Cold and Cough Remedy
just_in.excerpt: The Patanjali chairman’s prescription for cold season: warm milk, turmeric and a pinch of black pepper — supportive care backed by real pharmacology, but not a cure.
just_in.image_caption: Acharya Balkrishna. He describes turmeric milk as Ayurveda's traditional remedy for colds and coughs.
just_in.nri_angle: Diaspora families heading into cold season get a practical Ayurvedic remedy from Acharya Balkrishna — warm turmeric milk — with honest caveats about what it can and cannot do.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Dairy Valley Paneer Launches in Sainsbury’s and Tesco After Historic Cheese Awards Gold
just_in.excerpt: The first paneer ever to win Gold at the International Cheese & Dairy Awards goes on sale in Sainsbury’s next week, with Tesco in November — paneer’s big mainstream-UK moment.
just_in.image_caption: Paneer. Dairy Valley Paneer has launched in Sainsbury’s and Tesco.
just_in.nri_angle: Britain’s Indian community gets paneer that tastes like home in mainstream supermarkets, as a Gold-winning authentically made paneer lands in Sainsbury’s and Tesco.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: An Indian Family’s Dal Makhani Finds a Home on the French Riviera
just_in.excerpt: The family-run Mantraah in Nice’s Old Town serves dal makhani, tandoori naan and paneer to rave reviews — including repeat dinners three nights running.
just_in.image_caption: Dal makhani. An Indian family’s dal makhani has found a home on the French Riviera.
just_in.nri_angle: An Indian family’s restaurant bet on the French Riviera taps the diaspora’s universal longing for home food — and shows Indian cuisine finding new audiences in unexpected places.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Asia Society Texas Brings Diwali Lights Back to Houston on October 18
just_in.excerpt: The free, family-friendly festival of lights returns to the Texas Center in the Museum District on October 18, with food, fashion, crafts and a Ramayana performance — three weeks before Lakshmi Puja.
just_in.image_caption: Diwali lights. The Asia Society Texas festival returns to Houston on October 18.
just_in.nri_angle: Houston’s large Indian-American community gets one of its earliest Diwali-season celebrations of 2026 at Asia Society Texas’s free “Diwali Lights!” festival on October 18.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Shree Charani and Shafali Verma Power India Into Asian Games Cricket Semifinal
just_in.excerpt: India chased 58 in five overs to beat Japan by eight wickets in Nisshin, setting up a Sunday semifinal with Bangladesh, while the mixed doubles teqball pair reached the bronze-medal match.
just_in.image_caption: Shafali Verma and Shree Charani starred as India crushed Japan in the Asian Games women’s T20 quarter-final at Nisshin. Charani took 4 for 10 and Shafali hit 40 not out off 15 balls as India reached the semifinal with an eight-wicket win.
just_in.nri_angle: India’s Asian Games title defence in Nagoya is a headline story for the global Indian diaspora, from fans in Japan to the large Indian communities in the US following the Games.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Grated Veggies, Blended Tofu: A 23-Gram Protein Savoury Pancake Recipe
just_in.excerpt: Fitness influencer Vanshika Khurana's savoury pancake folds shredded vegetables and blended tofu into a rice-flour batter — a 23-gram-protein recipe she shared on Instagram on September 8.
just_in.image_caption: Savoury pancakes are pictured. The recipe packs 23 grams of protein into each serving using grated vegetables and blended tofu.
just_in.nri_angle: For Indian readers the savoury pancake feels instantly familiar — it is essentially a vegetable-loaded cheela rebuilt with silken tofu and a soy-lemon dip, a crossover that suits diaspora kitchens cooking across cuisines.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Wipro Launches STO360 With Aramco, SAP as Stock Slips Toward Nifty Exit
just_in.excerpt: Wipro's new STO360 platform, co-developed with Aramco and SAP, modernizes shutdown and outage management for asset-heavy industries — but the launch arrives as shares scrape a 52-week low and the company prepares to exit the Nifty 50 on September 30.
just_in.image_caption: A Wipro office is pictured. The company launched its STO360 platform with Aramco and SAP as its stock faces a possible Nifty exit.
just_in.nri_angle: Wipro is a bellwether of the Indian IT model built on offshore delivery, and its Nifty exit marks the first time in three decades the benchmark has dropped one of India's original software giants.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Sashi Cheliah, MasterChef Australia Winner, to Judge Celebrity MasterChef Tamil
just_in.excerpt: The 2018 MasterChef Australia champion joins the judging panel of the Samantha Ruth Prabhu-hosted celebrity spin-off, a launch title for Sony Pictures Networks India's new Tamil channel, Sony VIZHA.
just_in.image_caption: Chef Sashi Cheliah, the MasterChef Australia winner, is pictured. He will take a judge's seat on Celebrity MasterChef Tamil.
just_in.nri_angle: Sashi Cheliah — Singaporean-born, of Coimbatore-origin family, based in Adelaide — brings the diaspora's culinary success story full circle by judging Tamil celebrities on Sony VIZHA.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: From Oracle's Offices to a Karur Kiosk: Falooda Brand Hits Rs 9 Crore
just_in.excerpt: Pradeep Kannan walked away from a Rs 1-lakh-a-month operations role at Oracle in 2019 to open a 10×10-foot falooda kiosk in his hometown. Seven years on, The Falooda Shop has 18+ outlets across India and Dubai and revenue above Rs 9 crore.
just_in.image_caption: This image from StartupPedia illustrates the falooda entrepreneur story. Founder Pradeep Kannan left Oracle to sell falooda, and the brand now makes Rs 9 crore.
just_in.nri_angle: The brand's Dubai outlet and franchise model make it directly relevant to Gulf-based NRIs, both as customers and potential franchise investors, as Kannan eyes global expansion.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Bapuji Cake: West Bengal's ₹8 Tiffin Icon Still Sells 50,000 a Day
just_in.excerpt: New Howrah Bakery's humble square of buttered sponge has fed West Bengal's tea breaks since 1973 — handmade, sold for a handful of rupees, and still moving tens of thousands of pieces a day.
just_in.image_caption: A Bapuji cake is pictured. The Rs 8 West Bengal tiffin icon still sells 50,000 pieces a day.
just_in.nri_angle: For Bengali expats, Bapuji Cake is potent nostalgia — the taste of school tiffin boxes and platform tea stalls that travels home in suitcases and is now listed on Indian e-commerce for buyers outside Kolkata.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Aaryavir Sehwag Debuts, Anvay Dravid Fires as India U-19 Edge Australia by Seven Runs
just_in.excerpt: Yashvardhan Chauhan's 54 and 2 for 28 led the way, with debutant Aaryavir Sehwag (28) and Anvay Dravid (38 off 18) starring in a rain-shortened first Youth ODI against Australia at the Niranjan Shah Stadium in Rajkot.
just_in.image_caption: India's U-19 cricketers are pictured in this KhelNow photograph. Aaryavir Sehwag and Anvay Dravid starred as India beat Australia by seven runs in Rajkot.
just_in.nri_angle: For NRI families, watching the sons of Virender Sehwag and Rahul Dravid play for India U-19 collapses two decades of cricket nostalgia into one game, while youth cricket remains the route many diaspora parents use to pull their children into the sport.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: El Niño puts India on course for driest monsoon since 2009
just_in.excerpt: Rainfall is running 15% below the long-term average with less than two weeks left in the season, threatening crop yields and food prices in the world's biggest rice-producing country.
just_in.image_caption: A photograph from The Hindu BusinessLine. India is headed for its driest monsoon since 2009 as El Nino conditions take hold.
just_in.nri_angle: With rice export prices at their highest in more than a year, NRIs are likely to see Indian grocery bills climb abroad while families back home face rising food costs.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A Century Ago, the House of Saud Seized Mecca and Medina
news.excerpt: How Abdulaziz ibn Saud's 1924–1925 conquest of the Hejaz ended more than a thousand years of Hashemite custodianship of Islam's holiest cities — and reshaped the Hajj for the century that followed.
news.image_caption: A historical image of the holy cities from Saudipedia. The article recounts how the House of Saud seized Mecca and Medina from Hashemite rule a century ago.

news.title: AIIMS' Homegrown AI for Breast Cancer Detection Moves Toward Hospitals
news.excerpt: AIIMS Delhi has transferred its mammography AI — trained entirely on Indian data — to BPL Technologies for regulatory approval and hospital deployment.
news.image_caption: A mammography screening in progress. The AI tool developed at AIIMS Delhi acts as a second reader of mammograms, flagging possible signs of breast cancer for radiologists.
news.nri_angle: Breast cancer is the most common cancer among Indian women in cities; a homegrown AI screening aid built on Indian data is a milestone for Indian medtech that diaspora physicians and patients will watch.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's First Dengue Vaccine Could Reach Private Hospitals in Early 2027
news.excerpt: Dr Reddy's will distribute Takeda's Qdenga in India's private market from early 2027 — the first dengue vaccine approved in a country that carries a third of the global burden.
news.image_caption: An Aedes mosquito feeds on human skin. Dengue infects hundreds of millions of people globally each year, with India carrying nearly a third of the disease burden.
news.nri_angle: NRIs visiting India during monsoon season face dengue risk every year; a first vaccine arriving in 2027 changes the calculus for family travel.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: El Niño Raises Kerala Dengue Risk, IITM Study Finds; Cases Could Rise 20% by 2040
news.excerpt: A 14-year IITM analysis links Pacific warming to Kerala's dengue years — and the forecasting model behind it could warn health authorities five months ahead.
news.image_caption: Researchers at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras. An IITM study found El Niño’s warming effect could raise dengue cases 20% in some Indian cities by 2040.
news.nri_angle: Dengue surges hit Kerala's families — and the diaspora that travels home during monsoon season — making advance forecasting a lifeline for return visits.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Saudi Aramco Halts Crude Supplies to India as Pipeline Shutdown Bites
news.excerpt: With the East-West pipeline down, the kingdom's state oil company has told Indian refiners no term crude is coming — forcing expensive spot-market replacements.
news.image_caption: A Saudi Aramco oil facility. Aramco halted crude supplies to Indian refiners after a pipeline shutdown disrupted shipments.
news.nri_angle: Higher crude costs feed directly into India's import bill and fuel prices, squeezing the remittance value and household budgets of NRIs tied to the Indian economy.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Air India Weighs Folding Budget Arm AI Express Into Parent Group to Trim Losses
news.excerpt: Incoming CEO Tewolde Gebremariam has questioned why the Tata carrier runs two separate airline companies, arguing a single group would lower regulatory costs and duplicate management.
news.image_caption: An Air India aircraft on the tarmac. Air India is weighing folding its budget arm AI Express into the parent group to trim losses.
news.nri_angle: The Indian diaspora — among the world's most frequent flyers on India routes — would feel any restructuring through fares, network consolidation, and service reliability at the Tata carrier.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Canada Weighs Winding Down 41-Year Kanishka Bombing Probe, Drawing Anguish From Victims' Families
news.excerpt: The RCMP briefed victims' families on plans to scale back the investigation into the 1985 Air India bombing; families have written to PM Mark Carney demanding the probe be renewed, not retired.
news.image_caption: Wreckage from Air India Flight 182 recovered from the Atlantic after the June 23, 1985 bombing. Victims' families were briefed on September 12 about a possible move to scale back the 41-year-old RCMP investigation.
news.nri_angle: The bombing killed 268 Canadians, largely of Indian origin; the probe's fate is deeply personal to the Indo-Canadian diaspora and sits at the centre of strained India-Canada relations.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Asian Games Chief Calls Container Rooms 'Functional' as OCA Defends Scrapping Athletes' Village
news.excerpt: Organising committee president Hideaki Omura promised fixes as delegations complain of short beds, leaking huts and long waits — while the OCA says a traditional village would have been a costly white elephant.
news.image_caption: Container-style accommodation units for athletes at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games. Organising committee president Hideaki Omura called the rooms 'functional' amid complaints about cramped quarters and short beds.
news.nri_angle: Indian athletes faced 14-hour waits and missing registrations at the Nagoya Games, and the accommodation row is unfolding just as India's teams begin their medal campaigns.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Sikh Truck Driver Stabbed 17 Times at Wyoming Rest Stop, Suspect Charged
news.excerpt: The 28-year-old Sacramento driver was followed into a restroom at the Bitter Creek Rest Area along I-80 in the early hours of Sept. 13 and airlifted to a Casper hospital; Andrew Kris Bzdak, 45, was arrested and charged with attempted first-degree murder.
news.image_caption: Interstate 80 in Wyoming. The Sikh truck driver was attacked at the Bitter Creek Rest Area along the highway in Sweetwater County on Sept. 13; the suspect was charged with attempted first-degree murder.
news.nri_angle: A Sikh long-haul trucker from California's diaspora community was nearly killed on a U.S. highway days after federal immigration rhetoric mocked a turbaned Sikh driver, forcing Sikh Americans to confront the physical risks of anti-South Asian hostility.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Russian Missile and Drone Barrage Across Ukraine Injures at Least 19
news.excerpt: Overnight strikes on Kyiv, Zaporizhzhia and Odesa land days after Trump's claim of an energy-truce deal — while Ukraine hits a Russian refinery and airbase in return.
news.image_caption: Firefighters work below a Kyiv residential apartment building with shattered windows in the aftermath of a Russian strike. At least 19 people were injured in Russian missile and drone attacks across Ukraine on September 17.
news.nri_angle: Indian students and workers remain in Ukraine, and an Indian citizen was killed in a Russian strike on Boryspil outside Kyiv earlier this month, according to Reuters.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Trump Says Houthis Asked US to Stay Out as They Seize Red Sea Chokepoint
news.excerpt: President Trump said Yemen's Houthis asked Washington not to intervene even as the Iran-backed group seized control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait — putting a second major energy chokepoint under threat and driving oil above $100 a barrel.
news.image_caption: President Donald Trump walks across a tarmac in front of Marine One at dusk. In Dublin on September 12, Trump said Yemen's Houthis had asked the US not to intervene against them even as they seized control of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait.
news.nri_angle: Indian seafarers crewing merchant ships through the Red Sea face heightened risk, and sustained $100-plus oil with higher freight costs hits Indian consumers and importers directly.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Indian-Origin Texas Lab Owner on US Fugitive List Over $93M Medicare Fraud
news.excerpt: Khadeer Khan Mohammed, 46, is accused of billing Medicare $93 million for genetic tests doctors never ordered; HHS investigators say the alleged fugitive may be in Hyderabad, India.
news.image_caption: Khadeer Khan Mohammed. The Richardson, Texas lab owner is on the HHS-OIG fugitive list over 3 million in alleged fraudulent Medicare claims. (Photo: HHS-OIG)
news.nri_angle: An Indian-origin name on a U.S. federal fugitive list draws outsized attention in the Indian-American community — heavily represented in the very healthcare fields this alleged fraud exploited — even though the charges remain allegations.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: House Passes Graham Russia Sanctions Bill 262-159, Putting India in 100% Tariff Crosshairs
news.excerpt: Named for the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, the package authorises President Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the top importers of Russian energy; the Kremlin said Thursday the move would 'complicate' Ukraine peace efforts.
news.image_caption: The dome of the US Capitol in Washington, DC, with the American flag flying. The House of Representatives passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act by 262-159 on Wednesday, sending it to President Trump for his signature.
news.nri_angle: India is directly in the bill's crosshairs — New Delhi's Russian oil purchases could expose Indian exports to tariffs of up to 100%, and India has already warned Washington that such measures would damage bilateral ties.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Warns US That New Tariffs Over Russian Oil Could Damage Ties
news.excerpt: Hours after the US House passed a bill authorizing tariffs of up to 100% on top Russian oil buyers, New Delhi cautioned Washington that the move could strain the bilateral relationship and vowed to protect its energy security.
news.image_caption: An image from Mint's coverage of US-India trade relations. India warned on September 17 that a US House bill authorizing tariffs of up to 100% on buyers of Russian oil could damage bilateral ties.
news.nri_angle: For the diaspora, the standoff touches Indian-American importers, energy and trade professionals, and the US-India commercial corridor, all of which would feel the impact if the tariff weapon is actually deployed.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Finneas, Other Acts Quit Ed Sheeran Tour After Macklemore Ousted Over Palestine
news.excerpt: Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham and Sheeran's own touring band Beoga walked out on Tuesday, accusing stadium owners led by Robert Kraft of silencing the rapper's onstage "Free Palestine" remarks.
news.image_caption: Singer-songwriter and producer Finneas O'Connell. He quit Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour after Macklemore was dropped from the lineup.
news.nri_angle: For Indian-diaspora readers, the fallout is another reminder of how sharply pro-Palestinian speech is policed on Western pop's biggest stages.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Von der Leyen Pledges EU 'Counter-Hybrid Playbook,' Offers Canada Associate Membership
news.excerpt: In a 73-minute State of the Union address in Strasbourg, the European Commission president unveiled a European 'Article 4' emergency security protocol, a tougher stance on China, and a frontier-AI pact — warning that threats are mounting on European soil.
news.image_caption: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. She proposed a 'counter-hybrid playbook' for EU states facing sabotage and drone incursions.
news.nri_angle: The speech signals tighter EU borders and faster migrant returns alongside expanded legal migration channels and skills initiatives, a mix that matters for the Indian professionals and students who form one of the largest migrant communities in several EU states.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Galwan War Film's Long Road Shows India's Softening Line on China
news.excerpt: Salman Khan's Maatrubhumi — announced as Battle of Galwan — has been stalled by a defence ministry directive as India recalibrates its China policy, and TRT World says the saga reads like a barometer of that thaw.
news.nri_angle: The saga shows how New Delhi's China reset is reaching beyond diplomacy into the stories Bollywood is allowed to tell — a shift diaspora audiences will feel on screen before they see it in policy.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.excerpt: After SpaceX's June 12 debut minted new millionaires, Brian Aggrey and Phoebe Novack quit their jobs and set a $25,000-a-month budget for 365 days of chasing everything from acting school to sculpture — an experiment they call their "Year of Freak."
nri-world.image_caption: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket with a Dragon capsule rolls out to the launch pad. The company's record IPO has put the spotlight on a 14-year employee funding a year of dreams.
nri-world.nri_angle: The couple has no stated Indian connection, but their equity windfall mirrors the options-driven mobility that drew generations of Indian engineers to Silicon Valley — and SpaceX's IPO turned that possibility into real capital for employees across the org chart.

nri-world.title: IIT Madras Students' Crewless Vessel Wins Global Njord Challenge in Norway
nri-world.excerpt: Team Aritra beat 22 teams from nine countries at the autonomous ship competition in Trondheim, building on its 2023 podium finish.
nri-world.image_caption: IIT Madras Director Prof. V. Kamakoti with members of Team Aritra and their autonomous surface vessel. The ocean engineering students won the 2026 Njord Challenge in Trondheim, Norway, beating 22 teams from nine countries.
nri-world.nri_angle: IIT Madras students beat 22 teams from nine countries in marine robotics, another marker of Indian engineering talent winning on the world stage.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Krishnamoorthi Breaks With Indian-American Democrats on Russia Sanctions Vote
nri-world.excerpt: The Illinois Democrat was the sole Indian-origin House member to back the Graham sanctions bill carrying 100% tariff authority on Russian oil buyers including India.
nri-world.image_caption: U.S. Rep. Raja Krishnamoorthi. The Illinois congressman broke with fellow Indian-American Democrats on a Russia sanctions vote.
nri-world.nri_angle: Krishnamoorthi's vote puts a senior Indian-American lawmaker on the opposite side of a bill that could hit India with 100% tariffs over Russian oil — a fault line the diaspora will debate.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Turns to Diaspora in Nagoya as Asian Games Accommodation Crisis Deepens
nri-world.excerpt: With athletes evacuated from flooded container rooms and India's shooting team left waiting until 3 a.m., some 2,000 Indians in Nagoya stand ready to open their homes.
nri-world.image_caption: Nagoya at night, host city of the 2026 Asian Games. The city is facing an accommodation crunch that has pushed India to lean on its diaspora.
nri-world.nri_angle: The Indian diaspora in Japan is literally opening its homes to athletes, turning a host-organiser failure into a showcase of community mobilization.
